But while the mayor’s unorthodox media strategy has gotten scrutiny, not enough attention has been paid to the influencers themselves and their views.

Some in the mayor’s coterie are relatively innocuous. But others celebrate the assassination of Charlie Kirk, claim America runs “mass concentration camps,” and make apologies for terrorist attacks targeting synagogues.

These influencers can hardly be said to represent New Yorkers. Hundreds of posts from those identified as belonging to the group chat of the Mamdani administration media team have been devoted to police and prison abolition, dismantling Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and lambasting Israel. The content belies the mayor’s polished image as a moderate and offers more evidence that his social and professional circles are more radical than he lets on.

Mamdani has embraced influencer communications since taking office in January. “We need to speak to New Yorkers through every single medium that they see themselves and see the world around them, and all of you are such critical parts of that,” he said at an influencer-only summit hosted during his first week in office.

Joining Mamdani’s influencer brigade is easy, the CJR reported. After filling out an intake form, influencers receive “daily updates, talking points, and clips” through the “NYC Creators Announcements” group chat on the encrypted-messaging platform Signal. The initiative is led by Emilia Rowland, who serves as the mayor’s director of New Media and Cultural Communications.

Until two weeks ago, posts on that chat were set to auto-delete, in apparent violation of state record-keeping rules. Pro-Mamdani posters have found themselves scoring interviews with the mayor and, more significantly, positioning themselves to secure paid sponsorships promoting the work of government agencies.

In a statement to City Journal, Rowland said that “the Mayor’s office has never paid a content creator or influencer, full stop.” She added that “We engage broadly and in good faith, including with people who may disagree with the administration or have made comments the administration disagrees with—just as we allow outlets with a variety of partisan slants access to cover the mayor.”

City Hall has not published a complete list of the influencers included in the Signal chat. But my analysis of the 33 who could be identified found 18 on the Left or far Left, with an additional 15 posting primarily nonpolitical and occasionally political content.

For some of the influencers welcomed into the group chat, radical rhetoric is common. Framing the Israel–Hamas war as a “genocide,” presenting the police as racial oppressors, and suggesting that ICE is a “tool of fascism” are just some of the themes shared between members of the group chat and the Mamdani administration. Prominent far-left figures include Christina Brown. Brown, who goes by @missxtinab on Instagram, celebrated the assassination of Charlie Kirk (“violence was an answer”), suggested that ICE agents should be poisoned, and told her 282,000 followers, “I don’t love this country. I hate it so much. I want to see it fall.”

The Gallo-Roman Dodecahedron as a Multifunctional Ludic Artifact
A New Framework for Ancient Gambling Dynamics
Abstract
The true purpose of the hollow, copper-alloy Gallo-Roman dodecahedron remains one of archaeology’s most enduring mysteries, with hypotheses ranging from specialized textile tools to religious relics. This paper proposes a unifying premise: the dodecahedron was designed intentionally as a sophisticated, multi-role gambling device. By analyzing the structural characteristics common to discovered specimens—specifically the twenty vertex knobs, twelve pentagonal faces, and non-standardized, varying aperture diameters—we argue that the object functioned as a centralized mechanic for dynamic games of chance. Rather than serving a singular utilitarian or astronomical purpose, the physical geometry allows the artifact to simultaneously act as a multi-sided die, a kinetic randomizer, and a gateway for token- or stake-passing games. This framework accounts for the lack of contemporary written records, the variations in regional sizing, and the distribution of finds across high-activity social zones like military camps and baths. Viewing the dodecahedron as a complex ludic instrument provides a highly plausible, comprehensive explanation for its design and socio-cultural presence in the ancient world. The physical toss and the camp setting are argued from the object and the find-spots. The even/odd house split presented in §7 is a working reconstruction (Rule Set A), not a recovered ancient ordinance.
1. THE FRONTIER ENGINE
The Roman dodecahedron was an expensive, specialized metallurgical device used for gambling and high-stakes betting by gently tossing it on the ground and making it roll to a stop, combining the forward momentum of a bowling ball with the soft, unpredictable tumbling of standard dice. For centuries the academic community has shrouded this artifact in mystical ambiguity, but a cold analysis of its physical data reveals a tool built for the logistics of ancient frontier gaming.
To understand its design is to understand the laws of geometry and field usability. While minor styling differences exist between the rugged, utilitarian models cast in Roman Britain and the ornate pieces found in Gallo-Roman workshops, the underlying mathematical blueprint remains unified. This paper skips speculative mysticism and presents the case for a universal frontier gaming engine.
2. THE GAMING THEORY
When compared with standard academic papers, historians often look at the dodecahedron and see a beautiful, mysterious religious object. The approach here is different: look at how much money and engineering they poured into making a tavern gambling die that would not shatter on the first roll.
2.1 THE ROMANS WERE NOTORIOUS GAMBLERS
The ancient Romans were obsessed with gaming. Because gambling was technically illegal in the empire except during Saturnalia, soldiers and citizens became clever at hiding or adapting their games. Civilians in Rome hid dice games in secret rooms; soldiers on the cold remote frontiers developed games suited to a harsh environment. Roman legions were already familiar with structured gaming. Ludus Latrunculorum (The Game of Little Bandits) was a tactical battle on a grid using wax, stone, or glass pieces. Duodecim Scripta (Twelve Lines) is the direct ancestor of modern backgammon. Because running a gambling den was a punishable crime, boards were disguised: six words of six letters carved onto tavern benches. A famous board read: “To hunt, to bathe, to play, to laugh—this is to live!” To a passing centurion it looked like a poem; to the soldiers it was a 36-space racetrack.
Tabula dropped the middle row of Duodecim Scripta and looks almost identical to a modern backgammon board. Emperor Claudius loved the game enough to have a custom board built into his imperial carriage. Three dice went into a cone-shaped throwing cup (fritillum) or a miniature dice tower with internal steps to stop cheaters. The best throw was three sixes, the Venus Throw; the worst was the Dog Throw. Other games included Tali (knucklebones), Terni Lapilli, and the Nut Game.
To understand the dodecahedron one must understand the social fabric of the Imperial Roman Army. The core unit was the contubernium—eight soldiers who shared a tent, a cooking pot, a pack mule, and a life-or-death bond. Far from Rome, on frozen frontiers, these men formed an insular brotherhood: loyal on the battlefield, aggressively competitive in downtime. Gambling was not merely a distraction; it was a social ritual. Fleecing a fellow soldier was understood as a test of wit among brothers who trusted each other with their lives. It is within this culture of shared risk that the dodecahedron finds its context—not as a sacred artifact or a delicate measuring device, but as a robust instrument of chance, psychological manipulation, and tavern theater.
3. WHERE THE OBJECT WAS FOUND
No dodecahedron has ever been found in Rome or in Italy. Researchers have recorded approximately 130 specimens, concentrated in:
BRITANIA. During the main era of use (2nd–3rd centuries AD) the island was split into Britannia Inferior (the northern frontier toward Hadrian’s Wall) and Britannia Superior (the more heavily occupied south).
GALLIA. The region of the more ornate pieces: Gallia Lugdunensis, Gallia Belgica, and Gallia Aquitania.
GERMANIA. Rome never held the vast German interior. Finds cluster on the industrialized military border along the Rhine and Danube: Germania Inferior (lower Rhine) and Germania Superior (upper Rhine toward Switzerland).
Figure 1. Three Gallo-Roman dodecahedra showing provincial variation in knob shape, wall thickness, and face ornament. The shared twelve-face / twenty-knob blueprint is constant; execution is local.
3.1 Regional clusters
The British cluster (“rugged utility”). Finds such as Norton Disney in Lincolnshire tend to be heavier and cleaner in line. Corner knobs are often spherical and uniform; faces frequently carry sharp concentric rings around the apertures. The vibe is military hardware: solid, precisely cast, fewer decorative flourishes.
The Gallo-Roman cluster (“artisanal”). France and Belgium produce the most ornate casts. Knobs may be elongated or tapered; faces sometimes carry geometric borders. This matches pre-Roman Celtic bronze traditions merged with Roman technique.
The Germanic frontier cluster (“heavy alloy”). Camps along the Rhine and Danube favor thick-walled casting. Metallurgical testing often shows a high-lead bronze (leaded gunmetal) that poured smoothly into complex wax molds and finished darker and heavier—built to survive frontier weather and rough handling.
Approximate counts: France / ancient Gaul about 60; Great Britain about 33; German frontier about 30; remaining finds scattered through the Low Countries and the Alpine corridor. Different regional guilds manufactured distinct versions of a shared geometric blueprint. The object was not a centralized imperial mandate from Rome. It was an open-source mathematical concept that local cultures adopted and built in their own style.
As mapped in published distribution studies and supported by The Antiquaries Journal, the spatial pattern of the 130+ artifacts skews away from the imperial core. Regional fragmentation matches provincial manufacture rather than a decree radiating from Rome.
4. MANUFACTURING: ONE BLUEPRINT, MANY WORKSHOPS
Ancient Roman dodecahedra were cast as a single hollow copper-alloy piece by the lost-wax technique. An artisan sliced wax into twelve pentagons, cut the varying holes, fused them into a hollow shell, and attached twenty tiny wax balls at the vertices. A liquid clay mixture formed an interior core; thick clay coated the outside. Firing baked the clay and melted out the wax, leaving a thin hollow geometric cavity for the bronze pour.
4.1 Why twelve faces, not twenty?
An icosahedron would roll more smoothly on packed dirt, a blanket, or a tabletop. It was not chosen. Fusing twenty tiny triangles in wax without warping the angles is drastically harder than joining twelve wide pentagons. Pentagons have structural integrity; tiny triangles collapse. When molten bronze is poured into a twenty-sided mold, the metal must negotiate a maze of sharp intersections. Air pockets and freeze-offs become likely.
Space mathematically forbids a regular 18- or 24-faced polyhedron. For a regular, highly symmetrical, omnidirectional chassis, the dodecahedron is the ceiling of flat-faced stability. A twenty-faced chassis would also hit a resolution barrier: incremental differences among twenty holes on small triangular faces would be too fine to read by eye without a caliper. Twelve faces give a roll that settles on a stable pentagon and keep enough visual contrast between hole sizes for instant identification.
Figure 2. A single copper-alloy specimen. Unequal apertures, concentric rings, and twenty vertex knobs are visible in one view. In the reconstruction used here, the up-facing hole is read as the score.
The twelve holes progress from smallest to largest and, in Rule Set A below, serve as the point count. The side that lands up is the value. Every specimen subjected to 3D imaging or X-ray radiography has proven to be a continuous single hollow pour.
There are no internal welded or soldered seams. Frontier metal guilds pulled off a flawless single-pour hollow geometry without a metropolitan royal studio. They chose single pouring because a soldered game piece would crack when tossed repeatedly onto hard ground.
4.2 Impact dynamics and fairness
If knobs or faces had been soldered from separate parts, the seams would be fault lines. Tossed onto stone bathhouse tables or packed earth, a multi-part object would shatter. The single-pour bronze skeleton absorbs shock. Reheating edges to solder also introduces uneven density and micro-porosity. In a high-stakes game an unevenly weighted object is a liability—or, as argued below, a tool. Filling the mold, knobs included, in one pour produces a chassis whose weight distribution is at least internally consistent.When the northern frontiers collapsed in the early fourth century and military payrolls ceased, the three-century gambling craze vanished with its market.
5. PHYSICAL USER INTERFACE AND ARTISAN CONSTRAINTS
Classical interpretations often isolate the dodecahedron as a symbolic or abstract mathematical curiosity. Material analysis shows a tighter fit between structure and use.
5.1 Two-dice numerical mapping
A critical harmony exists between twelve faces and the bounds of two six-sided dice. Two cubes produce totals from 2 (1+1) to 12 (6+6): eleven discrete combined values. Condensed into one twelve-sided unit, the dodecahedron maps the span of a dual-dice system into a single object that can be used on rough surfaces without a matching pair.
5.2 Concentric rings as visual UI
Incised concentric rings around the openings are not mere ornament. In low light, small differences in hole diameter are hard to judge. Varying ring counts act as a high-contrast index of class or scoring value. No tactile measurement and no literacy are required.
5.3 Casting risk
Complex crests or Roman numerals cut into a twelve-sided wax model trap air and cause premature cooling. Concentric rings can be scribed on a rotating wax model with a compass or simple lathe tool. The design maximizes visual utility and minimizes failed casts.
6. WHERE AND WHEN THE GAME WAS PLAYED
A remote auxiliary fort on Hadrian’s Wall is the cleanest anchor for the boredom that drove soldiers to gamble.
Chesters Roman Fort (ancient Cilurnum), or nearby Housesteads, was active for about three centuries—the same span as the dodecahedron fad.
Figure 3. Reconstruction of Chesters Roman Fort (Cilurnum) on the North Tyne: walled cavalry fort, bridge, bath range, and the large extra mural vicus of streets and tiled houses. Site context, not proof of play. The scale of the civilian settlement undercuts the picture of a handful of cold auxiliaries knitting socks in the rain.
Located miles from any major civilian metropolis, these outposts were garrisoned by auxiliaries from Spain, Belgium, Syria and elsewhere—men taken from sunny climates and dropped into the damp hills of northern Britain. A garrison of roughly 500 cavalrymen could spend months without a combat engagement. After morning drill and construction, duty went empty. The luxury-tier bathhouse and dining ranges on the North Tyne were survival gear against psychological decay. Inside heated rooms—and, more privately, inside a shared tent after dark—high-stakes betting was the currency of escape. The dodecahedron was built for that setting: heavy, balanced bronze that could be tossed without shattering and read at a glance. A public daylight toss in the middle of a settlement is the least likely stage. The cleaner fit is a closed space: contubernium tent, bath anteroom, or tavern corner.
7. PLAYING THE GAME AND THE POINTS COUNT
Note - No ancient source preserves the scoring. Hole diameters are not numbered on the objects. What follows is a working reconstruction: one playable rule-set that fits twelve faces, a visible size-order, a house edge, and a fast craps-like settle.
Other mappings of the twelve faces remain possible. This paper uses RULE SET A so the mechanics can be tested, not because Rule Set A has been recovered from the ground.
In the reconstruction, the owner treats the object as a side business. It stays locked away until it appears in the circle; then everyone knows the game is on. In Rule Set A the twelve apertures are read in size order as values 1 through 12: smallest up-face = 1, largest = 12.
Rule Set A assigns the six even values (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12) to the players and the six odd values to the operator. Players may therefore believe they have half the wheel. The operator keeps the other half. That split is a model of house advantage, not a documented Roman ordinance. After the pot is in, players pick one or more of the six even values. The dodecahedron is rolled. If 4 comes up, those who picked 4 split the pot. If 7 comes up, the pot belongs to the house under this model. Players feel they have a fair 50/50 shot. Over time the house takes most of the table—especially if the object is slightly heavy on one side and the owner knows which side.
Alternative reconstructions—size-only pots with no banker, opposite-face pairs, or a marked subset of holes—would settle differently and are not excluded by the metal. The toss can be demonstrated. The parity split cannot.
7.1 House advantage and variable weight:
Six playable faces out of twelve look like even money. If odds belong to the house under Rule Set A, the math favors the owner. Because every face has a different hole diameter, remaining metal mass is uneven. Center of gravity is not perfectly centered. An owner who knows which face the cast prefers can fade the opposite bets all evening.
A 10,000-roll illustration: if weight bias gives each odd face only a 2-point lift (10.33% instead of 8.33%) and each even face a matching cut (6.33%), the evening becomes roughly 62% house wins versus 38% player wins. The table below is that illustration, not a claim that any one museum specimen was measured to these exact frequencies.
Table 1. Illustrative 10,000-roll split if odd (house) faces are each given a 2-point probability edge under Rule Set A. Totals: house faces 6,228 hits; player faces 3,772 hits. Not a laboratory measurement of a named specimen.
SEE IMAGE 3
7.2 Mechanics of play (Rule Set A)
ANTE AND CHOICE -  Before the cast, coins go on a surface or grid of even integers: II, IV, VI, VIII, X, XII. Illusion of equity. Half the point values look playable, so the average gambler calculates even money.
THE ROLL - Right knee down, short low underhand release from an open palm—the sidewalk craps toss, not a flick. Twenty spherical knobs produce an erratic, prolonged tumble that looks chaotic and masks any feel for the weight bias. The object slides out of the palm, drops a few inches onto packed dirt or a cloak, rolls, and stops with one face up.
SETTLEMENT UNDER RULE SET A - Even face up: those who backed that value split the pot. Odd face up: declared null for the public; the house sweeps the table. Alternative reconstructions would settle differently and are not excluded by the metal.
STRUCTURAL BIAS - Asymmetrical hollows leave different remaining mass. Gravity offsets toward faces with smaller holes. An operator who knows that physics can vacuum a camp or tavern over a long session.
8. WHY THE CRAZE VANISHED
The sudden disappearance of the dodecahedron in the late third and early fourth centuries is itself evidence of a specialized military gambling engine. The device did not fade. It vanished when its market was withdrawn. As the Western Empire contracted, legions were recalled from Britannia and Rhine outposts were dismantled or overrun.
The well-paid, bored soldiers left. Provincial foundries lost the clientele that paid for twelve-faced hollow casts.
What remains are buried relics of a three-century craze frozen in the soil of Rome’s lost borders.
9. WHY AUTHORS OF THE ERA NEVER WROTE ABOUT IT
SUETONIUS (c. 69–122) wrote endlessly about palace gambling by emperors. Tacitus (c. 56–120) wrote Germania on the same northern borders where the objects are found.
CASSIUS DIO (c. 155–235) wrote eighty volumes of Roman history. Ammianus Marcellinus (c. 330–395) chronicled Rhine and Danube campaigns. None of them mentions the dodecahedron
CLASS - These writers belonged to the senatorial or equestrian elite of the Mediterranean core. Day-to-day pastimes of auxiliary troops and frontier taverns were beneath formal Latin literature—low-brow provincial metalwork.
LAW - Gambling (alea) was illegal outside Saturnalia. Governors and centurions were supposed to enforce the edict. A specialized illegal betting device would not appear on Vindolanda-style inventories or in an officer’s dispatch to the capital.
GEOGRAPHY - Zero specimens in Italy. Writers in Rome had no reason to know the object existed. It was a provincial, open-source phenomenon confined to Britannia, Gallia, and Germania.
The silence of contemporary literature is not a mystery. It is a predictable consequence of Roman class structure and imperial law. The lack of written records does not prove the device was a sacred mystery; it is consistent with an illicit, localized frontier gaming piece that never crossed a senator’s desk.
10. THE ALIBI HYPOTESIS
If a legionary were caught with a dodecahedron during inspection, he needed a plausible story. Given Roman bathing and athletic habits, a useful defense was that the object was a health tool: a gift for deep-tissue work after long marches. Used with bath oil, the vertex knobs function as rollers for back, neck, and shoulders. A commander facing an odd geometric object and a medical excuse could dismiss it as an eccentric grooming accessory. Once the excuse worked, it would travel the network. That would help explain finds in baths and the total omission from official chronicles.
This socio-legal scenario is speculative and is offered only as an interpretive hypothesis. It is one cultural mechanism that can reconcile physical distribution with literary silence.
NOTES FROM THE AUTHOR
The game, even treated as a behavioral study, answers why these objects turn up near camps, taverns, and towns where soldiers and merchants had cash and time. Accounts of meager frontier life—soldiers knitting their own socks—are often written for drama. The Imperial army demanded respect. Men at Chesters were fed, housed, and linked to Rome by roads and mail. Many came from families that sent packages. Serving the empire was an honor, not a sentence to destitution. Stakes were not only denarii. Inside the contubernium men wagered wine rations, care-package goods, and unofficial claims in the local civilian economy.
In closing: the strongest claim this paper makes is functional. It was a gambling device, expensive to make, exclusive (about 130 known, and possibly not many more ever made), handled by gamblers. It was treated with care when not in use—like a pool player’s cue in a case, or a golfer’s own clubs. Played at a fast pace like craps, money changing hands, all illegal. Many specimens were found with personal belongings, coin hoards, and amulets. Some were found smashed. The even/odd house split is the counting used here so the object can be played and tested. It is not presented as the recovered Roman statute.
Figures retained: museum photographs of actual artifacts (Figs. 1–2) and one site reconstruction of Chesters (Fig. 3).
Atmospheric AI reconstructions were omitted as non-evidentiary. Table 1 is an illustrative model of house edge under Rule Set A, not a laboratory measurement of a named specimen. This version is the latest and  revises §7 so scoring language is marked as reconstruction.

5.1 Two-dice numerical mapping
A critical harmony exists between twelve faces and the bounds of two six-sided dice. Two cubes produce totals from 2 (1+1) to 12 (6+6): eleven discrete combined values. Condensed into one twelve-sided unit, the dodecahedron maps the span of a dual-dice system into a single object that can be used on rough surfaces without a matching pair.
5.2 Concentric rings as visual UI
Incised concentric rings around the openings are not mere ornament. In low light, small differences in hole diameter are hard to judge. Varying ring counts act as a high-contrast index of class or scoring value. No tactile measurement and no literacy are required.
5.3 Casting risk
Complex crests or Roman numerals cut into a twelve-sided wax model trap air and cause premature cooling. Concentric rings can be scribed on a rotating wax model with a compass or simple lathe tool. The design maximizes visual utility and minimizes failed casts.
6. WHERE AND WHEN THE GAME WAS PLAYED
A remote auxiliary fort on Hadrian’s Wall is the cleanest anchor for the boredom that drove soldiers to gamble.
Chesters Roman Fort (ancient Cilurnum), or nearby Housesteads, was active for about three centuries—the same span as the dodecahedron fad.
Figure 3. Reconstruction of Chesters Roman Fort (Cilurnum) on the North Tyne: walled cavalry fort, bridge, bath range, and the large extra mural vicus of streets and tiled houses. Site context, not proof of play. The scale of the civilian settlement undercuts the picture of a handful of cold auxiliaries knitting socks in the rain.
Located miles from any major civilian metropolis, these outposts were garrisoned by auxiliaries from Spain, Belgium, Syria and elsewhere—men taken from sunny climates and dropped into the damp hills of northern Britain. A garrison of roughly 500 cavalrymen could spend months without a combat engagement. After morning drill and construction, duty went empty. The luxury-tier bathhouse and dining ranges on the North Tyne were survival gear against psychological decay. Inside heated rooms—and, more privately, inside a shared tent after dark—high-stakes betting was the currency of escape. The dodecahedron was built for that setting: heavy, balanced bronze that could be tossed without shattering and read at a glance. A public daylight toss in the middle of a settlement is the least likely stage. The cleaner fit is a closed space: contubernium tent, bath anteroom, or tavern corner.
7. PLAYING THE GAME AND THE POINTS COUNT
Note - No ancient source preserves the scoring. Hole diameters are not numbered on the objects. What follows is a working reconstruction: one playable rule-set that fits twelve faces, a visible size-order, a house edge, and a fast craps-like settle.
Other mappings of the twelve faces remain possible. This paper uses RULE SET A so the mechanics can be tested, not because Rule Set A has been recovered from the ground.
In the reconstruction, the owner treats the object as a side business. It stays locked away until it appears in the circle; then everyone knows the game is on. In Rule Set A the twelve apertures are read in size order as values 1 through 12: smallest up-face = 1, largest = 12.
Rule Set A assigns the six even values (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12) to the players and the six odd values to the operator. Players may therefore believe they have half the wheel. The operator keeps the other half. That split is a model of house advantage, not a documented Roman ordinance. After the pot is in, players pick one or more of the six even values. The dodecahedron is rolled. If 4 comes up, those who picked 4 split the pot. If 7 comes up, the pot belongs to the house under this model. Players feel they have a fair 50/50 shot. Over time the house takes most of the table—especially if the object is slightly heavy on one side and the owner knows which side.
Alternative reconstructions—size-only pots with no banker, opposite-face pairs, or a marked subset of holes—would settle differently and are not excluded by the metal. The toss can be demonstrated. The parity split cannot.
7.1 House advantage and variable weight:
Six playable faces out of twelve look like even money. If odds belong to the house under Rule Set A, the math favors the owner. Because every face has a different hole diameter, remaining metal mass is uneven. Center of gravity is not perfectly centered. An owner who knows which face the cast prefers can fade the opposite bets all evening.
A 10,000-roll illustration: if weight bias gives each odd face only a 2-point lift (10.33% instead of 8.33%) and each even face a matching cut (6.33%), the evening becomes roughly 62% house wins versus 38% player wins. The table below is that illustration, not a claim that any one museum specimen was measured to these exact frequencies.
Table 1. Illustrative 10,000-roll split if odd (house) faces are each given a 2-point probability edge under Rule Set A. Totals: house faces 6,228 hits; player faces 3,772 hits. Not a laboratory measurement of a named specimen.
SEE IMAGE 3
7.2 Mechanics of play (Rule Set A)
ANTE AND CHOICE -  Before the cast, coins go on a surface or grid of even integers: II, IV, VI, VIII, X, XII. Illusion of equity. Half the point values look playable, so the average gambler calculates even money.
THE ROLL - Right knee down, short low underhand release from an open palm—the sidewalk craps toss, not a flick. Twenty spherical knobs produce an erratic, prolonged tumble that looks chaotic and masks any feel for the weight bias. The object slides out of the palm, drops a few inches onto packed dirt or a cloak, rolls, and stops with one face up.
SETTLEMENT UNDER RULE SET A - Even face up: those who backed that value split the pot. Odd face up: declared null for the public; the house sweeps the table. Alternative reconstructions would settle differently and are not excluded by the metal.
STRUCTURAL BIAS - Asymmetrical hollows leave different remaining mass. Gravity offsets toward faces with smaller holes. An operator who knows that physics can vacuum a camp or tavern over a long session.
8. WHY THE CRAZE VANISHED
The sudden disappearance of the dodecahedron in the late third and early fourth centuries is itself evidence of a specialized military gambling engine. The device did not fade. It vanished when its market was withdrawn. As the Western Empire contracted, legions were recalled from Britannia and Rhine outposts were dismantled or overrun.
The well-paid, bored soldiers left. Provincial foundries lost the clientele that paid for twelve-faced hollow casts.
What remains are buried relics of a three-century craze frozen in the soil of Rome’s lost borders.
9. WHY AUTHORS OF THE ERA NEVER WROTE ABOUT IT
SUETONIUS (c. 69–122) wrote endlessly about palace gambling by emperors. Tacitus (c. 56–120) wrote Germania on the same northern borders where the objects are found.
CASSIUS DIO (c. 155–235) wrote eighty volumes of Roman history. Ammianus Marcellinus (c. 330–395) chronicled Rhine and Danube campaigns. None of them mentions the dodecahedron
CLASS - These writers belonged to the senatorial or equestrian elite of the Mediterranean core. Day-to-day pastimes of auxiliary troops and frontier taverns were beneath formal Latin literature—low-brow provincial metalwork.
LAW - Gambling (alea) was illegal outside Saturnalia. Governors and centurions were supposed to enforce the edict. A specialized illegal betting device would not appear on Vindolanda-style inventories or in an officer’s dispatch to the capital.
GEOGRAPHY - Zero specimens in Italy. Writers in Rome had no reason to know the object existed. It was a provincial, open-source phenomenon confined to Britannia, Gallia, and Germania.
The silence of contemporary literature is not a mystery. It is a predictable consequence of Roman class structure and imperial law. The lack of written records does not prove the device was a sacred mystery; it is consistent with an illicit, localized frontier gaming piece that never crossed a senator’s desk.
10. THE ALIBI HYPOTESIS
If a legionary were caught with a dodecahedron during inspection, he needed a plausible story. Given Roman bathing and athletic habits, a useful defense was that the object was a health tool: a gift for deep-tissue work after long marches. Used with bath oil, the vertex knobs function as rollers for back, neck, and shoulders. A commander facing an odd geometric object and a medical excuse could dismiss it as an eccentric grooming accessory. Once the excuse worked, it would travel the network. That would help explain finds in baths and the total omission from official chronicles.
This socio-legal scenario is speculative and is offered only as an interpretive hypothesis. It is one cultural mechanism that can reconcile physical distribution with literary silence.
NOTES FROM THE AUTHOR
The game, even treated as a behavioral study, answers why these objects turn up near camps, taverns, and towns where soldiers and merchants had cash and time. Accounts of meager frontier life—soldiers knitting their own socks—are often written for drama. The Imperial army demanded respect. Men at Chesters were fed, housed, and linked to Rome by roads and mail. Many came from families that sent packages. Serving the empire was an honor, not a sentence to destitution. Stakes were not only denarii. Inside the contubernium men wagered wine rations, care-package goods, and unofficial claims in the local civilian economy.
In closing: the strongest claim this paper makes is functional. It was a gambling device, expensive to make, exclusive (about 130 known, and possibly not many more ever made), handled by gamblers. It was treated with care when not in use—like a pool player’s cue in a case, or a golfer’s own clubs. Played at a fast pace like craps, money changing hands, all illegal. Many specimens were found with personal belongings, coin hoards, and amulets. Some were found smashed. The even/odd house split is the counting used here so the object can be played and tested. It is not presented as the recovered Roman statute.
Figures retained: museum photographs of actual artifacts (Figs. 1–2) and one site reconstruction of Chesters (Fig. 3).
Atmospheric AI reconstructions were omitted as non-evidentiary. Table 1 is an illustrative model of house edge under Rule Set A, not a laboratory measurement of a named specimen. This version is the latest and  revises §7 so scoring language is marked as reconstruction.

🚨 Pakistan Recruiting Former Afghan Soldiers and Police for Operations in Balochistan:

RADIO FREE EUROPE REPORTS SAY:

Pakistan is recruiting former Afghan army and police personnel to fight armed groups in Balochistan.

Those recruited are reportedly being paid around 40,000 Pakistani rupees per month.

A former Afghan soldier said he was also offered a position with Pakistani security agencies. 

According to him, the offer came through a former police officer of the previous Afghan government who had previously recruited hundreds of former Afghan police personnel.

Another source monitoring militant activity in the region claimed that nearly 2,000 former Afghan police officers and soldiers have been recruited in Balochistan.

However, a former Afghan soldier said the actual number could be even higher.

According to the report, the recruits are introduced to local police so they can carry weapons and pass through security checkpoints without facing difficulties.

They are reportedly paid approximately 40,000 Pakistani rupees per month.

The allegations come as Balochistan faces increasing attacks by Baloch separatist groups and the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

Earlier, the Melbourne Asia Review reported in a research article that accounts from the region indicate Pakistan is using some former Afghan security personnel and jihadist commanders in what it described as a new phase of proxy warfare.

In late August, Fazal Qadir Mandokhail, a local member of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam, told the Balochistan Provincial Assembly that thousands of former Afghan soldiers had been brought into the province.

Abdul Qahir Wadan, the Balochistan leader of the Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party, said the presence of former Afghan soldiers and police officers in Balochistan is “no longer a secret.”

However, the Balochistan provincial government said it has no confirmed evidence that thousands of former Afghan soldiers have been brought into the province.

The Pakistani military also did not respond to Radio Free Europe’s questions.

If the reports of recruitment are confirmed, they could further complicate the already strained relations between Kabul and Islamabad.

For anyone wondering about context (yes, it's AI generated, but we watched each of these things play our in real time, this is just summarizing and reviewing known facts):

Trump became financially dependent on an industry his own administration regulates. Trump’s 2025 financial disclosure reported more than $1.4 billion in income from family crypto ventures: nearly $800 million from World Liberty Financial and about $635 million from the Trump memecoin. Although his businesses are managed through a trust, Trump remains the beneficiary. At the same time, his administration has changed crypto enforcement and regulation, including SEC, DOJ and banking policy. That creates the basic conflict: presidential policy can materially affect the value of businesses producing enormous personal income for the president. (Reuters)

The $TRUMP memecoin created an unusually direct mechanism for sending money toward a sitting president's financial interests. Trump launched $TRUMP three days before his January 20, 2025 inauguration. Trump-linked CIC Digital and Fight Fight Fight initially controlled roughly 80% of the token supply. Unlike an ordinary business selling a product at a relatively stable price, people could buy large quantities of a token whose price was tied closely to Trump's name, publicity and political power. Reuters later estimated hundreds of millions in revenue for Trump-linked entities. (Reuters)

The memecoin was explicitly turned into a mechanism for purchasing presidential access. In 2025, the 220 largest qualifying $TRUMP holders were invited to dinner with President Trump at his Virginia golf club; the top 25 received a VIP reception. Investors spent an estimated $148 million competing for those positions, and more than half appeared to be based outside the United States. The original promotion even referred to a VIP White House tour before that language was removed. Trump repeated the model in April 2026: the top 297 holders were invited to Mar-a-Lago and the top 29 received a VIP reception and champagne toast with the president. (Reuters)This is different from a campaign fundraiser. Money spent buying $TRUMP was not a regulated campaign contribution subject to normal contribution limits and donor-disclosure rules; it supported an asset from which Trump-linked businesses financially benefited.

Crypto wallets make the foreign-influence problem much harder to police. Many large $TRUMP and WLFI holdings are pseudonymous. That means a foreign billionaire, company or potentially a government-connected entity can acquire millions of dollars of Trump-linked crypto without the public necessarily knowing the beneficial owner. Reuters found that foreign buyers represented a large portion of major WLFI holders and that most million-dollar buyers were hidden behind wallet addresses. That creates an influence channel considerably less transparent than traditional campaign donations or lobbying. (Reuters)

Justin Sun is one of the clearest examples of the overlap between money, presidential access and federal enforcement. The SEC sued Sun in 2023, accusing him and his companies of unregistered securities sales, wash trading/manipulation and undisclosed celebrity promotions. Sun subsequently invested at least $75 million in World Liberty Financial, became a WLFI adviser and became the largest publicly known $TRUMP dinner participant. After Trump returned to office, the SEC case was paused; in March 2026 the SEC agreed to a resolution under which one Sun company would pay $10 million while the remaining claims against Sun and the other Tron defendants were dismissed. Sun and his companies did not admit wrongdoing. (Securities and Exchange Commission)There is no established evidence that Sun purchased the SEC outcome, so it would be inaccurate to call this proven bribery. The conflict is that a person facing enforcement by Trump's SEC simultaneously became one of the largest financial supporters of Trump's private crypto interests and obtained personal access to Trump.

Sun's TRON connection adds a national-security/illicit-finance dimension. Reuters previously reported that TRON had become heavily used in crypto transfers associated with groups including Hamas and Hezbollah and had been targeted in Israeli and U.S. enforcement actions. That does not establish that Sun personally financed terrorism, but it makes the relationship more consequential because his business operated in an area directly touching U.S. sanctions, anti-money-laundering and national-security enforcement. (Reuters)

The UAE/Sheikh Tahnoon deal creates a much more direct foreign-government conflict. Four days before Trump's 2025 inauguration, a company backed by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan — the UAE's national security adviser and brother of the UAE president — agreed to pay $500 million for a 49% stake in World Liberty Financial. Reporting indicates roughly $187 million of the initial payment went to Trump-family entities and at least $31 million to Witkoff-linked entities. (The Washington Post)This matters differently from an ordinary foreign investor because Tahnoon is simultaneously a senior official of a foreign government with major matters before the U.S. government.

The UAE crypto investment overlapped with an extremely sensitive U.S. national-security decision involving AI chips. Tahnoon also chairs G42 and MGX. U.S. officials had previously restricted advanced AI-chip access because of concerns about UAE technology relationships with China. After Trump returned to office, his administration substantially expanded UAE access to advanced American AI technology. The sequence — a UAE national-security official backing a $500 million investment in Trump's family company followed by favorable U.S. decisions concerning strategically sensitive technology — has prompted requests for CFIUS and congressional investigation. (Reuters)Again, the chronology establishes a conflict, not proof that Trump exchanged chip policy for money. There is currently no publicly established quid pro quo. But unlike a normal domestic regulatory conflict, this one involves a foreign government's national-security chief, Trump's personal finances and U.S. control of technology central to competition with China.

The UAE then provided a massive boost to World Liberty's USD1 stablecoin. MGX, the Abu Dhabi state-controlled investment company chaired by Tahnoon, used $2 billion of World Liberty's USD1 stablecoin to make an investment in Binance. That transaction accounted for most of USD1's circulation at the time. Reuters calculated that reserves associated with the stablecoin could generate roughly $80 million annually in interest, with Trump-linked entities participating in the economics. (Reuters)This therefore wasn't simply "the UAE bought crypto." A foreign state-controlled entity selected a financial product tied to the sitting president's family for a multi-billion-dollar transaction while the president controlled U.S. foreign policy toward that same country.

The Binance/CZ pardon creates another unusually tight sequence of intersecting interests. Binance pleaded guilty in 2023 to Bank Secrecy Act, money-transmission and U.S. sanctions offenses and paid about $4.3 billion. Founder Changpeng "CZ" Zhao separately pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program and served nearly four months in prison. DOJ said Binance's failures allowed money to flow through the platform involving terrorists, cybercriminals and sanctioned activity. (Department of Justice)

Then MGX invested $2 billion in Binance using Trump's USD1. CZ publicly acknowledged applying for a presidential pardon. On October 23, 2025, Trump pardoned him. (Reuters)

Binance and Zhao have expressly denied that the MGX/USD1 transaction had anything to do with the pardon, and there is no public proof of such a bargain. But the sequence creates an obvious conflict question: a company financially supporting adoption of the president's family's stablecoin had a founder seeking extraordinary relief that only the president could grant.

The Binance issue also has a genuine national-security component, not merely a regulatory one. DOJ's Binance prosecution involved sanctions and anti-money-laundering failures and was jointly handled with the Justice Department's National Security Division. DOJ said Binance was required to review historical transactions partly to aid investigations involving cybercrime and terrorism financing, including Hamas. That background makes the pardon more consequential than an ordinary white-collar clemency case. (Department of Justice)

Trump also pardoned the BitMEX founders and executive. In March 2025 Trump pardoned Arthur Hayes, Benjamin Delo, Samuel Reed and Gregory Dwyer, who had pleaded guilty to Bank Secrecy Act/anti-money-laundering offenses involving BitMEX. (Reuters)

This is relevant to Trump's broader relationship with the crypto industry, but I would not put it in the same factual category as CZ. I have not found evidence tying the BitMEX pardons directly to payments into Trump's own crypto businesses.

Ross Ulbricht's pardon similarly demonstrates Trump's clemency toward prominent crypto-associated figures, but there is no documented personal financial connection. Trump pardoned Silk Road founder Ross Ulbricht shortly after taking office. Ulbricht had been convicted of narcotics trafficking, operating a continuing criminal enterprise, computer-hacking conspiracy, false-document trafficking and money laundering; Silk Road relied extensively on Bitcoin. (Department of Justice)

Trump had promised the pardon publicly to Libertarian supporters during the campaign. So it belongs in the wider crypto/pardon story, but available evidence does not establish that Ulbricht enriched Trump or his family.

World Liberty also received a $100 million investment from an opaque purported UAE fund whose ownership Reuters could not establish. Aqua 1 Foundation announced a $100 million WLFI purchase in June 2025. Reuters could find essentially no conventional corporate history for Aqua 1, could not establish the source of its money and found it was not registered with the Abu Dhabi financial center where it said it planned to operate. Because the Trump family received three-quarters of WLFI token-sale proceeds under the arrangement then in effect, the purchase sent tens of millions toward Trump-family interests. (Reuters)

The concern here isn't that Aqua 1 has been proved to be a foreign-government front; that has not been established. The problem is that tens of millions can flow from an opaque foreign entity toward a sitting president's family without the public knowing whose money it ultimately is.

Steve Witkoff's dual role adds another foreign-policy conflict around World Liberty. Witkoff co-founded World Liberty alongside the Trump families before becoming one of Trump's most important Middle East diplomatic envoys. His family remained deeply tied to the business. His 2025 disclosure later showed more than $100 million in income from an entity connected with World Liberty, while the Tahnoon investment reportedly sent at least $31 million to Witkoff-linked entities. (The Wall Street Journal)

That creates a separate issue from Trump's own finances: one of the officials conducting sensitive American diplomacy in the Middle East had a family financial connection to a company receiving enormous sums from a senior UAE royal and national-security official. The White House says Witkoff's prior business interests did not affect his diplomatic work.

Trump's NFTs established the "spend money, get personal access" model even before the memecoin. Buyers of Trump's "Mugshot Edition" NFTs who bought enough tokens were invited to a May 2024 dinner at Mar-a-Lago; people who spent roughly $10,000 buying 100 NFTs were offered a VIP cocktail reception. One foreign buyer explicitly told Axios that the attraction was the opportunity to meet Trump. Trump subsequently reported continuing NFT licensing income; his 2025 disclosure listed about $1.16 million from NFTs. (Axios)

Because the 2024 dinner happened while Trump was a candidate rather than sitting president, it is legally different from the $TRUMP dinners held after he returned to office. But it established essentially the same commercial model: purchases of a Trump product unlocking personal access to Trump.

World Liberty itself later received a federal banking approval from Trump's executive branch. On August 14, 2026, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted conditional preliminary approval for World Liberty Trust Company, N.A., allowing the Trump-family crypto enterprise to establish a federally chartered trust bank associated with USD1. The OCC says it followed its normal legal and supervisory process. (Reuters)

Even absent evidence that Trump intervened, a federal regulator granting a valuable charter to a business producing enormous income for the president's family is precisely the kind of situation traditional divestiture or a genuine blind trust is designed to avoid.

World Liberty has also mixed its private business events with federal policymakers and regulators. At its February 2026 World Liberty Forum at Mar-a-Lago, Trump sons and Witkoff sons hosted Wall Street executives alongside federal officials including the CFTC chairman and other Trump administration officials. Reuters described it as a convergence of Trump-family business interests, regulators, political appointees, lawmakers and financial firms with interests in crypto regulation. (Reuters)

The legal distinction is important. Federal criminal conflict-of-interest statutes such as 18 U.S.C. §208 traditionally do not apply to the president or vice president, according to the Office of Government Ethics. So saying "this is a conflict of interest" does not automatically mean "this violates §208." (USOGE)

Other laws and constitutional provisions can potentially apply. The Foreign Emoluments Clause was specifically intended to protect U.S. officials from foreign-government influence, and UAE state-connected payments to Trump-linked businesses have prompted arguments that the clause is implicated. But the Supreme Court never resolved the major Trump emoluments litigation from his first term on the merits, so the precise boundaries remain legally unsettled. (EveryCRSReport) Likewise, bribery would require evidence of an exchange of official action for something of value; the public record described above establishes troubling sequences and financial relationships, but does not by itself prove such a quid pro quo.

The unifying factual problem is therefore fairly simple: people and foreign governments with matters before the president can put very large sums of money into assets and companies from which the president and his family financially benefit, sometimes anonymously; some of those same people have received presidential access, regulatory relief, pardons, or favorable U.S. policy outcomes. The existence of those relationships is documented. Whether any particular favorable government action was caused by the corresponding financial relationship requires evidence beyond timing and financial benefit.

And this isn't merely retrospective controversy. As of September 15, 2026, the ethics problem has become part of the actual congressional fight over crypto regulation: the latest CLARITY Act negotiations included new restrictions aimed specifically at preventing federal officeholders from profiting from their own crypto ventures. (Reuters)

Wednesday, September 16, 2026

Walking in Light, Not in Craftiness
 
 Scripture Reading: I Peter 4:1-2 (“King James Version”)

1. Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind: for he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin;

2. That he no longer should live the rest of his time in the flesh to the lusts of men, but to the will of God.

Key Verse: II Corinthians 4:2 (“King James Version”)

2.  But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God.
 
Note to reader: All verses quoted are from "King James Version."

The Call to Open Honesty

Jehovah does not ask us to polish an image. He asks us to renounce what cannot bear the light. Hidden thoughts about another person, quiet envy, clever words used to win an argument, a private habit we would never name in prayer—these are the “hidden things of dishonesty.” They may never become public scandal, yet they train the soul in secrecy.

Craftiness is not merely lying. It is using a slanted word, a half-true story, a religious phrase, or a shrewd method to carry our point. The gospel will not travel that road. The Word of  Jehovah is not a tool for advantage. It is truth to be manifested.

Christ suffered in the flesh. Those who arm themselves with His mind refuse to let the old uses of the body—jealousy, strife, cunning—rise again. Watchfulness is not suspicion of others; it is honesty before  Jehovah about ourselves.

Never blunt the sense that  Jehovah has given you a particular call to utmost honesty. Another believer may act in a way that is lawful for them. If the same act would mean slyness in you, it is forbidden.  Jehovah has given you His standpoint. Do not draw back from it because it looks costly or lonely.

Inspiration from Faithful Voices

Oswald Chambers pressed this very text: have you renounced the things your sense of honor will not allow into the light? Renounce the thought as soon as it springs up, until nothing hidden, dishonest, or cunning remains. Never catch people by a method  Jehovah has not given you. Never dull “your utmost for His highest” by comparing yourself with others who work another way.

Charles Spurgeon warned that craft and treachery harden a heart against grace. He loved plain speech. Truth, he said, needs no apology if it is let loose; but a man who tampers with words, especially holy words, does not know where he will stop. The Word of  Jehovah must not be concealed, twisted, or used as a mask.

William Branham insisted that the test of any ministry, motive, or spirit is the Word itself—not sincerity alone, not results, not cleverness. He urged a clean heart, a right motive, and a refusal to add to or take from what  Jehovahhas said. Sincerity without the Word can still be wrong; the Word without sincerity is already dishonest.

Together they point to one life: open before  Jehovah, loyal to Scripture, free of the hidden things of shame.

How to Put This into Daily Life

Morning search. Pray Psalm 139:23–24 before the day begins. Name any thought you would not want spoken aloud.

Renounce at once. When envy, a sly reply, or a private accusation appears, refuse it in the moment. Do not nurse it “just this once.”

Speak without a second agenda. In conversation, teaching, correction, or online words, ask: Am I manifesting truth, or trying to win?

Do not handle Scripture as a weapon for self. Quote it as it stands. Do not trim a verse to protect your pride or to pressure another.

Keep one standard for hidden and public life. If it cannot be done in the sight of  Jehovah, do not do it in secret.

Suffer rather than scheme. When honesty costs you an advantage, take the loss. That is arming yourself with the mind of Christ.

Refuse comparison. Another’s liberty is not your license. Obey the light  Jehovah has given you.

Additional Scriptures for Mediation

II Corinthians 2:17  — “For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ.”

II Corinthians 1:12  — “For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world…”

Proverbs 10:9 — “He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.”

Jeffersonian vs Utilitarian

🟢 Maximizing Utility: The Positive View
A utilitarian would praise Jefferson’s deep distrust of centralized power and entrenched elites.
•Local Optimization: Jefferson believed that decisions should be made close to the people. Utilitarians agree that local rulers have better information to maximize the happiness of their specific communities than a distant bureaucracy.
•
•Democratic Participation: By expanding voting rights to a broader base of white males, Jeffersonianism increased the "utility" of the average citizen by giving them a stake and a voice in their own destiny.
•

🔴 Diminishing Utility: The Negative View
A utilitarian would severely criticize the systemic blind spots and economic outcomes of Jeffersonian policies.
•The Problem of Slavery: The most catastrophic utilitarian failure of the Jeffersonian era was its reliance on chattel slavery. The immense, agonizing suffering inflicted on enslaved populations completely erases the utility gains enjoyed by land-owning citizens.
•
•Economic Sub-optimization: Jefferson’s idealized agrarian society actively resisted industrialization and central banking (like Hamilton's economic plan). From a modern utilitarian perspective, industrialization, technological progress, and stable financial systems are essential to lifting millions out of poverty and raising the global baseline of human happiness. Jefferson's model would have kept society materially poorer.
•

🎯 The Verdict
A utilitarian would conclude that Jeffersonian Politics offers an excellent blueprint for individual liberty and local happiness, but falls short as a global model because it lacks the centralized efficiency, economic modernization, and universal human rights required to truly maximize the greatest good for the greatest number of people.

text:
Most Americans grow up hearing that enslaved people escaped by heading north.

But long before the Underground Railroad carried people toward Canada, there was another road to freedom.

It ran SOUTH.

In 1693, Spain offered freedom to enslaved Africans who escaped the British colonies and made it to Spanish Florida. They would swear allegiance to Spain, embrace the Catholic faith, and the able-bodied men would serve in the Spanish militia.

So men, women, and children began making the dangerous journey through hundreds of miles of forests, rivers, and swamps toward St. Augustine.

They were not simply escaping slavery.

They were walking toward freedom.

By 1738, Spain established Gracia Real de Santa Teresa de Mose, better known today as Fort Mose, just north of St. Augustine. It became the first legally sanctioned free Black community in what is now the United States.

And these men didn’t just receive their freedom.

They defended it.

Under the command of Francisco Menéndez, himself formerly enslaved, the Black militia at Fort Mose helped defend Spanish Florida against the British. In 1740, they fought in the bloody battle that drove British forces from the fort.

Think about that for a moment.

People who had once been property escaped hundreds of miles to Florida, became free citizens, built homes and families, worshipped as Catholics, carried weapons, and fought to defend the land that had given them freedom.

And today, at Fort Mose, you can still walk the path commemorating that journey.

For thousands of enslaved people, freedom wasn’t north.

Freedom was Florida.

Iran has been our enemy since the day I was born.  Pretend otherwise at your - our - peril.  

**No on overflight. Partial and qualified on the rest.** Iran did not petition to join a U.S.-led military coalition, did not offer overflight for combat operations in September 2001, and the pilot-recovery arrangement came later, after a U.S. request.

### Coalition / UN role
Iran condemned the 9/11 attacks and said it would support an **international** campaign against terrorism **if it were under UN leadership**. Foreign Minister Kamal Kharazi told Kofi Annan that the UN should be the “axis” of the effort so there would be international consensus. Iran was already in the UN “6+2” group on Afghanistan (the six neighbors plus the U.S. and Russia).

That is not the same as petitioning to join “our UN coalition” as a U.S. military partner. Iranian leaders repeatedly refused a U.S.-led campaign:

- Supreme Leader Khamenei said Iran would not take part in any measure led by the United States and would provide no help to America or its allies in an attack on Afghanistan.
- Kharazi said Iran would not participate in “the operations and the coalition led by the United States nor in the military component.”

Operation Enduring Freedom was a U.S.-led coalition under self-defense, not a UN-commanded force. Iran wanted UN political cover and a UN-shaped political settlement; it rejected joining the American military effort.

### Overflight
Iran **refused** overflight for U.S. warplanes attacking Afghanistan. In mid-to-late September 2001, the Foreign Ministry said it would never allow American aircraft to use Iranian airspace for that purpose. In early October the defense minister warned that repeated airspace violations would be treated as planned and confronted.

Iran kept its airspace closed to U.S. combat operations. That was public and consistent.

### Pilot recovery
This was **October, not September**, and it was a response to a U.S. request, not an unsolicited Iranian offer of basing or overflight.

After bombing began on 7 October, the U.S. sent a message (via Swiss intermediaries, who represent U.S. interests in Tehran) asking Iran to help if American personnel were shot down or forced to land in Iran. Iran agreed to search-and-rescue and return them. Secretary of State Powell confirmed that mid-October. U.S. officials also said they did not expect to need it, because they were not operating through Iranian airspace.

That was a limited, humanitarian/SAR understanding after the U.S. also assured Iran it would respect Iranian territorial integrity. It was not permission to fly combat missions over Iran.

### What Iran *did* do (broader context)
Iran and the Taliban were already enemies (1998 massacre of Iranian diplomats, support for the Northern Alliance). After 9/11 there was limited, mostly quiet cooperation: border closure, pressure on some militants, intelligence contacts, humanitarian routes, and later close work with U.S. envoy James Dobbins at the UN-sponsored Bonn conference in December 2001 on a post-Taliban government. That cooperation is well documented. It does not rewrite the September public record on coalition membership or overflight.

**Bottom line:** Iran offered UN-framed political cooperation and later agreed to recover downed U.S. personnel if they ended up on Iranian soil. It did not petition to join the U.S. military coalition and did not offer overflight rights in September 2001.

text:
Antigua and Barbuda at a Glance

Antigua and Barbuda is a twin-island nation in the eastern Caribbean, part of the Leeward Islands in the Lesser Antilles. It sits between St. Kitts and Nevis to the west and Guadeloupe to the south. The country consists primarily of Antigua, Barbuda, and the uninhabited island of Redonda. Antigua is famous for its claim of 365 beaches, one for every day of the year.

Location in the Caribbean

Antigua lies in the northeastern Caribbean Sea and is a popular yachting and cruise destination due to its protected harbors and warm climate year-round.

History
Indigenous Peoples

The islands were originally inhabited by Indigenous peoples, including the Arawaks and later the Caribs.

Colonial Era
Christopher Columbus sighted Antigua in 1493 during his second voyage.
Britain colonized Antigua in the 17th century.
Large sugar plantations developed, relying heavily on enslaved African labor.
Emancipation and Independence
Slavery was abolished throughout the British Empire in 1834.
Antigua and Barbuda gained full independence from the United Kingdom on November 1, 1981, while remaining a member of the Commonwealth.

Today, remnants of the colonial period remain visible at sites such as Nelson's Dockyard, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

People
Population: approximately 95,000 to 100,000
Official language: English
Ethnic composition: predominantly of African descent, reflecting the islands' plantation history.
Residents are known for their hospitality and relaxed Caribbean lifestyle.

The local nickname for Antiguans is**"Wadadli,"** an old indigenous name for Antigua.

Culture

Antiguan and Barbudan culture blends African, British, and Caribbean influences.

Music
Calypso
Soca
Reggae
Steel-pan music
Major Events
Antigua Carnival (summer), widely regarded as one of the Caribbean's premier carnivals.
Antigua Sailing Week, one of the world's leading sailing regattas.
Sports

Cricket is deeply embedded in national culture. Antigua is the birthplace of legendary cricketer Sir Vivian Richards.

Cuisine

Local cuisine combines African, British, and West Indian influences.

Must-Try Dishes
Fungee and Pepperpot (national dish)
Fresh lobster (especially in Barbuda)
Saltfish
Conch
Curried goat
Roti
Grilled mahi-mahi
Johnny cakes

Local beverages include:

Wadadli beer
Caribbean rum punches
Fresh tropical fruit juices
Beaches: How Do They Rank Globally?

Antigua's beach reputation is exceptional.

Notable beaches include:

Half Moon Bay
Dickenson Bay
Valley Church Beach
Ffryes Beach
Darkwood Beach
Long Bay Beach

The Antigua & Barbuda Tourism Authority notes that Half Moon Bay has been recognized as one of the world's premier beaches and is now a national park.

While no universally accepted global ranking exists for all beaches, travel publications and traveler reviews consistently place Antigua among:

The top beach destinations in the Caribbean
One of the best islands worldwide for beach variety
A contender alongside beach destinations such as Turks and Caicos, Bora Bora, the Maldives, Aruba, and Seychelles.
Best Beach Experiences
Beach Known ForHalf Moon Bay Natural beauty, photography
Dickenson Bay Resorts, water sports
Valley Church Beach Calm turquoise water
Ffryes Beach Soft sand and fewer crowds
Darkwood Beach Snorkeling and scenery
Barbuda Pink Sand Beaches Remote, pristine, nearly empty
Getting There from the Continental U.S.
Main Airport

V.C. Bird International Airport (ANU) on Antigua is the country's primary gateway. Numerous airlines provide service including American, Delta, JetBlue, United, and others.

Direct Flights Available

Direct service is commonly available from:

Miami
New York (JFK and Newark)
Atlanta
Charlotte

Many other U.S. cities connect through these hubs.

Flight Costs (Round Trip from Continental U.S.)

Approximate economy fares:

Departure Region Economy Premium Economy Business ClassEast Coast $400-$700 $800-$1,400 $2,000-$4,000
Midwest $500-$900 $1,000-$1,800 $2,500-$5,000
West Coast $700-$1,200 $1,500-$2,500 $3,500-$7,000

Prices vary substantially by season. December through April is high season.

Do You Need Additional Flights or Water Taxis?
Staying on Antigua

No. Most visitors:

Fly directly into ANU.
Take a 10 to 40 minute taxi ride to their resort.

No additional flights or ferries are required.

Visiting Barbuda

If you want to explore Barbuda during your trip, you'll need:

Option 1: Ferry

Approximately 90 minutes to 2 hours each way.
Day trips are common.

Option 2: Small Aircraft

About 20 minutes.
More expensive but convenient.
One-Week Vacation Costs
Couple (Mid-Range)
Category Estimated CostAirfare $1,000-$1,600
Hotel/Resort $2,000-$4,000
Food & Drinks $500-$1,000
Transportation $100-$300
Activities $300-$1,000
Total $4,000-$8,000

Independent travel averages around $5,700 for a couple for one week according to traveler spending data.

Family of Four (Mid-Range)
Category Estimated CostAirfare $2,000-$3,500
Accommodation $3,500-$7,000
Food $1,000-$1,800
Transport $200-$500
Activities $500-$1,500
Total $7,000-$14,000

Some travel-industry estimates place a typical family-of-four week in Antigua at roughly $12,000 when staying at an all-inclusive resort and including flights.

Bottom Line

Antigua and Barbuda is one of the easiest Caribbean destinations for Americans to visit. You can often fly directly from major U.S. cities, land on Antigua, and be at your resort within 30 minutes. No ferry or island-hopping is required unless you specifically want to visit Barbuda.

For travelers seeking beautiful beaches, warm water, English-speaking locals, rich Caribbean culture, and relatively easy access from the United States, Antigua and Barbuda is consistently considered one of the Caribbean's premier beach destinations.

🌺✨ 𝗝𝗨𝗦𝗧 𝟮𝟱 𝗗𝗔𝗬𝗦 𝗧𝗢 𝗚𝗢 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗔𝗟𝗨𝗥𝗨 𝗗𝗔𝗦𝗔𝗥𝗔! ✨🌺

The countdown has begun! Just 25 days to go for the beginning of Navaratri, and the beautiful coastal city of Mangaluru is getting ready to celebrate its grand and vibrant Dasara festivities.

Mangaluru Dasara is one of the most prominent and widely celebrated Dasara festivities in Karnataka after the world-famous Mysuru Dasara. During Navaratri and Dasara, Mangaluru transforms into a city of devotion, lights, culture and celebrations. Temples are beautifully decorated and illuminated, special poojas and cultural programmes are conducted and the entire city comes alive with the spirit of the festival.

The grandeur of Mangaluru Dasara can be experienced particularly at Kudroli Sri Gokarnanatha Kshethra, Shree Mangaladevi Temple and through the traditional Sharadothsava celebrations at Car Street. Each of these celebrations has its own history, traditions and unique atmosphere, making Mangaluru a special destination to experience Dasara.

🌺 𝗞𝗨𝗗𝗥𝗢𝗟𝗜 𝗦𝗥𝗜 𝗚𝗢𝗞𝗔𝗥𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗔𝗧𝗛𝗔 𝗞𝗦𝗛𝗘𝗧𝗛𝗥𝗔 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗔𝗟𝗨𝗥𝗨 𝗗𝗔𝗦𝗔𝗥𝗔

The spectacular Mangaluru Dasara celebrations at Kudroli Sri Gokarnanatha Kshethra are among the biggest attractions of the festival. During Navaratri, the temple premises are beautifully decorated and illuminated, with special religious rituals and cultural programmes taking place throughout the celebrations.

The worship of Goddess Sharada, Mahaganapati, Navadurgas and other deities forms an important part of the festivities. The grand Dasara procession on Vijayadashami is the major highlight, with beautifully decorated tableaux and idols accompanied by traditional chende, folk dances, Yakshagana, Dollu Kunitha, Gombe and the famous Pilinalike/Hulivesha.

The procession travels through the important streets of Mangaluru and attracts devotees and visitors in large numbers before returning to Kudroli Sri Gokarnanatha Kshethra.

🌺 𝗦𝗛𝗥𝗘𝗘 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗔𝗟𝗔𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗜 𝗧𝗘𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘 — 𝗔 𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗗𝗜𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗥𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗜𝗡 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗔𝗟𝗨𝗥𝗨

The historic Shree Mangaladevi Temple at Bolar is another important centre of Navaratri and Dasara celebrations in Mangaluru. The temple has a special place in the history and identity of the city, with Mangaluru itself deriving its name from Goddess Mangaladevi.

During Navaratri, devotees visit the temple in large numbers and participate in the special poojas and religious celebrations. The Vijayadashami celebrations and Rathotsava towards Marnamikatta are important parts of the traditional festivities associated with the temple.

🌸 𝗦𝗛𝗔𝗥𝗔𝗗𝗢𝗧𝗛𝗦𝗔𝗩𝗔 𝗔𝗧 𝗖𝗔𝗥 𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗘𝗘𝗧

The historic Car Street area has its own special charm during Navaratri. The traditional Sharadothsava at Acharya Math brings the area alive with devotion, religious programmes and cultural celebrations.

The worship of Goddess Sharada and the traditional procession through the streets of Car Street are important attractions of the Sharadothsava. The celebrations here showcase the rich religious and cultural traditions that have been preserved in Mangaluru for generations.

From the grandeur of Kudroli to the sacred traditions of Mangaladevi and the historic Sharadothsava of Car Street, Mangaluru offers visitors a unique experience during the Navaratri and Dasara season.

🚆✨ 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗧𝗢 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗔𝗟𝗨𝗥𝗨 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗗𝗔𝗦𝗔𝗥𝗔 — 𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗩𝗘𝗟 𝗕𝗬 𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗜𝗡! ✨🚆

Planning to experience Mangaluru Dasara this year?

Mangaluru is well connected by railway from Bengaluru, Hassan, Mysuru, northern Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra, Keralam, Tamil Nadu and several other parts of the country.

The city has two major railway stations — 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗿𝘂 𝗖𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗹 (𝗠𝗔𝗤) and 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗿𝘂 𝗝𝘂𝗻𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 (𝗠𝗔𝗝𝗡), both playing an important role in connecting Mangaluru with different parts of Karnataka and the country.

𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗿𝘂 𝗖𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗹 (𝗠𝗔𝗤) is the 𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗹𝘄𝗮𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗿𝘂 𝗰𝗶𝘁𝘆. It is located at Attavar–Hampankatta, in the centre of Mangaluru and close to the city's major commercial and prime areas. Its central location makes it particularly convenient for visitors arriving to experience the major Dasara celebration areas.

From Mangaluru Central, Acharya Math at Car Street, where the traditional Sharadothsava takes place, is around 1.7 km away, Kudroli Sri Gokarnanatha Kshethra is approximately 2.8 km away, and Shree Mangaladevi Temple is approximately 3.2 km away.

𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗿𝘂 𝗝𝘂𝗻𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 (𝗠𝗔𝗝𝗡) is located at Padil, behind the New DC Office area and is another major railway gateway to Mangaluru. It is an important 𝗷𝘂𝗻𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 for trains connecting Mangaluru with the Konkan Railway, Hassan–Mangaluru line and routes towards Keralam and Tamil Nadu, making it an important railway gateway for long-distance and regional train services.

From Mangaluru Junction, Kudroli Sri Gokarnanatha Kshethra is approximately 7 km away, Shree Mangaladevi Temple is around 5.6 km away and Acharya Math at Car Street is around 5.7 km away.

🚆 𝗙𝗥𝗢𝗠 𝗕𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗔𝗟𝗨𝗥𝗨 / 𝗛𝗔𝗦𝗦𝗔𝗡 𝗦𝗜𝗗𝗘

For passengers travelling from Bengaluru, Hassan and other parts of Karnataka through the Hassan-Mangaluru railway line, some important trains include:

🚆 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗡𝗼. 𝟭𝟲𝟱𝟭𝟭/𝟭𝟲𝟱𝟭𝟮 KSR Bengaluru–Kozhikode Express

🚆 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗡𝗼. 𝟭𝟲𝟱𝟴𝟱/𝟭𝟲𝟱𝟴𝟲 SMVT Bengaluru–Murdeshwar Express

This train also continues towards the Konkan Railway route up to Murdeshwar from Mangaluru.

🚆 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗡𝗼. 𝟭𝟳𝟯𝟳𝟳/𝟭𝟳𝟯𝟳𝟴 Vijayapura–Mangaluru Central Express

Another option is Train No. 16595/16596 KSR Bengaluru-Karwar Panchaganga Express. This train travels through this corridor but does not reach Mangaluru city. Passengers can get down at Surathkal or Bantwal and continue towards Mangaluru by road. Surathkal is approximately 17 km from Hampankatta, while Bantwal is approximately 23.7 km away.

🚆 𝗟𝗢𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗜𝗡𝗦 𝗙𝗥𝗢𝗠 𝗦𝗨𝗕𝗥𝗔𝗛𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗬𝗔 𝗥𝗢𝗔𝗗

For passengers travelling from Subrahmanya Road and the interior and rural areas of Dakshina Kannada, the Hassan–Mangaluru railway line itself provides an important local rail connection to Mangaluru. text:
THE INVISIBLE DISSOLUTION

It happens quietly. There is no grand ceremony or official turning point. You just wake up one morning and realize the television is playing a Thai broadcast, and you are actually following the plot. You open your fridge, and the imported steaks and frozen french fries are gone. Instead, there is an organized inventory of fish sauce, fresh holy basil, and precisely sorted chilies.

You go to the local wet market, and the vegetable stalls are no longer just a chaotic, intimidating pile of random green weeds. You know the exact name of every leaf. You know which ones go into a slow-cooked broth, which ones need to be stir-fried, and which ones are eaten raw. You don't need a guide to navigate the food stalls anymore. You walk into a shop, automatically kick off your sandals, and actually have to nudge your Thai partner to remind her to take her shoes off.

You have completely, silently dissolved into the ecosystem.

This phenomenon is fascinating because of the speed and absolute totality with which it consumes a specific type of foreigner. In sociology, this might be called acculturation or deep structural assimilation. But on the ground, it is simply the path of least resistance.

Thailand is unique because it offers a very stark choice to outsiders, and it absolutely does not care which one you pick.

The Two Operating Systems

On one side, you have the "20-Year Tourist." This is the guy who has lived here for two decades but still operates entirely within an imported simulation. He eats a heavy English breakfast of baked beans and sausages every single morning. He complains about the heat. He hasn’t learned a single word of Thai beyond ordering a beer and aggressively disputing a bill. The country completely allows this. Thailand will happily build you Irish pubs, air-conditioned Western supermarkets, and English-speaking enclaves. It will gladly take your money while keeping you permanently walled off from the actual mechanics of the society.

On the other side, you have the guys who experience the complete dissolution. Why does it work for them? Because they stop treating the country as a long-term holiday resort and start treating it as a functional reality.

They realize that fighting the local operating system is physically and psychologically exhausting. Trying to force Western logic onto Thai infrastructure is a recipe for a heart attack. So, they surrender. It is a "soft surrender." They learn the language because it removes daily friction. They trade the heavy bacon for a steaming bowl of khao tom (rice soup) in the morning because the local climate demands it. They adapt to the local rhythm because it is the only way the machine actually works.

The moment you stop fighting the current, the culture swallows you whole. The ultimate marker of this transition isn't just speaking the language or marrying a local. It is that quiet moment in the supermarket when you are the one reminding your wife that you need to buy more jasmine rice.
